clue.text: A hot pride galavanised goddess

indicators.note: galvanised means jolted into action, so the preceding letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A flushed, proud deity is jolted into action.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is printed 'galavanised', a slip for 'galvanised'; it carries no letters, so the anagram of A HOT PRIDE is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek deity of love and beauty.

clue.text: Sales-talk angle

definitions.meaning: the slope or inclination of something, as of a roof

explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is both a seller's patter and the degree of slope of a roof.

clue.text: Newcomer, that is, supporting swindle

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle them
IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A new arrival backs up a con trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice recruit just starting out.

clue.text: Edith right to come out in a state of indecision?

indicators.note: letters that come out of their places get scrambled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Edith is unsure whether she should reveal herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a dither means being flustered and unable to decide.

clue.text: Twisted roots of trunk

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gnarled roots belong to a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a tree, but trunk here is the human body without head or limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the main part of the body, its trunk.

clue.text: Knocking down lots of people, continue gear-changing!

indicators.note: letters that are changing shift around into a different arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder as printed, plus the single letter I the setter's wording has evidently lost

explanation.surface: A driver mowing down pedestrians keeps shifting gear.
explanation.walkthrough: As held, 'continue gear' is one I short of AUCTIONEERING; the clue presumably read 'I continue gear-changing', and 'changing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer sells lots by bringing down the hammer, so knocking down lots is that trade.

clue.text: French composer receives share of formal discussions

indicators.note: one piece receives another when it takes it inside itself

parts.note: Leo Delibes was the French composer of the ballet Coppelia
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A composer from France is handed his portion of the talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberations are careful debates, such as those of a jury or committee.

clue.text: Kipling's accounts set out with precision?

parts.note: something arranged exactly is arranged just so
stories are narrative accounts

explanation.surface: Kipling's tales are told with great exactness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote the Just So Stories, a children's book of animal fables.

clue.text: Fall guy has go at space-travelling

indicators.note: letters travelling move about from their places, a cue for rearrangement

explanation.surface: A patsy takes a shot at space flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is a person made to take the blame for others.

clue.text: Trick of doing something in art

definitions.text: Trick of doing something in art

parts.words: Trick of doing something in art
parts.note: the knack or method an artist uses to achieve an effect

explanation.definitionFit: Technique is the skill or method applied in performing or creating a work.

clue.text: Break in the voice for a musical round

definitions.meaning: a momentary crack or hitch when speaking or singing
a part-song in which voices enter in turn, often humorous

explanation.definitionFit: A catch is both a hitch in the voice and an old form of round sung by several voices.

clue.text: Woman, old, with bad back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for bad is written from right to left

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: An elderly lady has a painful back.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's given name.

clue.text: That man with skill and courage

parts.note: he refers to that man
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A man of talent and bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart is used for bravery, as in to take heart or lose heart.

clue.text: Female taking in the Spanish-Greek beauty

indicators.note: one piece taking in another holds it within

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A woman embraces a Spanish-Greek beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy was the legendary beauty whose abduction launched the Trojan War.

clue.text: Reportedly, a cereal bowl over

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, signalling a word that sounds like the following phrase

parts.note: a cereal crop is a maize

explanation.surface: A breakfast dish is said to be turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowl over' looks like a cereal bowl tipped up; it means astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish them.

clue.text: Plant poles in Scottish river

indicators.note: in places the poles within the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone plants posts in a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a yellow-flowered herb of the daisy family.

clue.text: Tailless nursery-bear led off with dog

indicators.note: an animal without its tail loses its final letter

parts.note: Pooh is the honey-loving bear of children's stories by A. A. Milne

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear without a tail is led away by a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' drops the final H of POOH; 'off' rearranges LED to DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The poodle is a curly-coated breed of canine.

clue.text: Once more, fares badly going to hospital

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the word before are put in a poor order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone does poorly again and ends up in a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew or again from the start.

clue.text: Pick up some of what in unclear, normally

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run within them

explanation.surface: We usually grasp a bit of what is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'uncLEAR, Normally'. 'what in' is presumably an OCR slip for 'what is'; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or language is to acquire it.

clue.text: Fat, would you say, of the land?

indicators.note: asking how one would say it points to a word that sounds like another

parts.note: grease is animal fat

explanation.surface: A question about the fat of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the phrase 'the fat of the land', meaning the best of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Sadly, I am going back for a banger

indicators.note: going back turns each of the two words for sadly and I am round, in place

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Unhappily, someone is heading home for a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns ALAS into SALA and IM into MI. In Britain a banger is slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spicy cured sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: Very poor, but brave marshal clutching two notes

indicators.note: one piece clutching another grips it inside

parts.note: Michel Ney, Napoleon's marshal, was called the bravest of the brave
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A courageous officer holds a pair of banknotes, though he is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy describes someone lacking the necessities of life, destitute.

clue.text: Thing carried by writer as errors appear

definitions.text: Thing carried by writer as errors appear

indicators.note: a thing carried by the words sits inside them, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A writer keeps a tool handy for mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'writER AS ERrors'; the whole clue also describes the object.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber for removing pencil or ink is what a writer reaches for to fix a slip.

clue.text: Realm in which to commit matricide?

definitions.text: Realm in which to commit matricide?

parts.words: Realm in which to commit matricide?
parts.note: a sphere of control, but split as slang it says kill mother inside

explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory or sphere ruled or controlled by someone.

clue.text: A right racket in this sort of quarrel?

parts.note: a racket is a din, a row

explanation.surface: A fair dispute over a noisy argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like an argument, but here it is the bolt shot from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of missile like a shaft from a bow.

clue.text: The way, endlessly, to grind grain

indicators.note: grinding breaks things up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the phrase is lost

explanation.surface: The path to milling corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the Y from THE WAY, leaving THEWA, which 'to grind' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal crop whose seed is milled for flour.

clue.text: Leave-taking, go out dressed in gold

indicators.note: a piece dressed in another is clothed by it, sitting inside

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a fire or light that goes out dies

explanation.surface: Someone leaves dressed in golden finery.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, said on parting.

clue.text: Great range of Danse Macabre?

indicators.note: macabre suggests something grotesque or distorted, so the word is reshaped

explanation.surface: The scale of Saint-Saens's Danse Macabre.
explanation.walkthrough: Danse Macabre is a famous orchestral piece; 'Macabre' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the great mountain chain of South America.

clue.text: Digging below station

parts.note: under means below
station means rank or standing in society

explanation.surface: Excavating beneath a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: Digging is slang for comprehension, from 'to dig', to get it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig is slang for to grasp, so digging is comprehension.

clue.text: Forbidding aspect of presenting rear to head?

indicators.note: to joins the rear and the head, putting one beside the other

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Turning your back to someone's face looks unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity of manner, a harsh look, is what forbidding conveys.
